findings.summary: Return-plan review command left ten product paths undecided, so the return would be refused; corrected to a verified --keep list.
Exclude rationale misdescribed the mechanism: .shiploop-improve is excluded by rule, not by reviewer decision.
Rollback recipes keyed on the pre-run baseline would undo the first return too; rebased onto the first-return SHA.
Release target bullet repeated the wrong base commit for main.
Step 1 did not say where the README check runs or that plan-return commits uncommitted work, shifting the head.
A13 settle said returned-tree confirmation happens at release-check, which runs before the return; reassigned to release-verify.
Four ST catalog rows claimed requirement clauses their cases never observe, overclaiming system-level coverage.
Accessibility N/A bullet attributed R-3.5 live clauses to ST-1, which does not observe them.
Release step 1 README requirement no longer matched ST-4's port-statement oracle, risking a release failing its own check.
ID-convention row for ST-4 omitted R-2.3 and the README clause.
Release-check ST-4 row and consumer check 2 absent output did not name a README dropping the port statement.
Spec acceptance status lacked a note recording what the second pass changed.
AD-6 built the cells in the inline script, contradicting R-3.1 and T-12; server-render them into the page string.
T-26 loading-state check could pass on a page whose script never ran.
T-32 pgrep listener check could not attribute a listener to the suite; replaced with in-suite assertions.
Helpers under test/support would be run as tests by node --test, letting pass>=1 hold with no real test.
T-30 exit-0 half is vacuous at base where node --test with no files exits 0.
T-33 command block failed before node ran because test/ directory is absent; added mkdir -p.
TC_BROWSER_WIN expected every cell to show a result, which cannot happen after the grid disables at game over.
Twelve acceptance lines had no check naming them; coverage mapping was only prose.
TC_BROWSER_LOCK had no ordered procedure.
TC_PORT_DEFAULTS miscounted starts and ignored an already-held port 3000/8081, so not replayable.
TC_BROWSER_ERROR would hang as written because server.close() waits for keep-alive sockets.
Test-count floor (at least 14 tests, 3 per file) was never shown reachable.
.gitignore missing from the file list although the suite writes profile files.
Step 2 gave an expected main SHA the plan's own commit had already falsified.
Step 1 claimed plan-return commits release-plan edits, no longer true after improve-commit.
Step 4 called a past SHA the current candidate.
Three ragged line wraps in the touched paragraphs.
TC_COORDINATES lacked the accept-at-extremes half of A-R5.2, so a clamping server would pass.
TC_GAME_OVER_REFUSAL did not require an unfired cell, so it could pass without reaching the game-over branch.
TC_RESOLUTION and TC_REPEAT_SHOT had no stated oracle for the 5 sunk, 12 hit split and repeat-hit rule.
TC_TWO_GAMES and TC_CONCURRENT_FIRE dropped A-R10.2 sequence and A-R10.5 shipsRemaining clauses.
TC_ERROR_TABLE fixtures could not produce non-UUID id, trailing-slash 404 and query-string rows.
R-4 cited research assumption A4 for UUID default; the actual source is R2/A5.
R-5 error list defined no precedence, leaving combined faults under-determined.
R-5.5 and TR-10 said the concurrent loser always gets already fired, false when the winning shot ends the game.
R-5.4 repeat-shot clause contradicted the post-game rule.
R-5 never required Content-Type application/json on /api/fire, leaving the header claim unverifiable.
R-3.2, R-3.3 and R-3.5 stated behaviour their confirmations did not check.
C-R5-3 oracle asserted an error-message wording that no criterion or accepted plan supports and named no substring.
Result summary attributed C-R2-3 to W2; the plan gives it to W3.
C-R5-3 GREEN ended with a next-valid-shot clause that no assertion checked.
Accepted step plan's S1 proof runs a test file written only after implement; recorded as open item, not fixed.
SYS-REL-1 expected output had a trailing slash after the port that the command does not print.
R-5.1 said fire every cell while R-5.4 rejects shots after game over; full-game check not replayable.
R-2.2 said empty PORT means 3000 but Number(PORT) maps empty to 0.
R-2.2/R-2.3 confirmation relied on binding port 3000 with a permitted skip, which is not evidence.
TR-6 and TR-7 gave two answers for a post-game repeat shot.
State inventory claimed a sunk ship's other cells render sunk, though the client never learns them.
R-3.1 accepted any title containing Battleship and named no stable cell selector.
F-2 had the player firing at cells of the last unsunk ship, which the player cannot know.
R-7.4 scratch failing test lay outside test/, so node --test would not discover it.
A2 was omitted from the Open gaps section.
Accepted result headline said 27 acceptance lines; the spec has 28.
Transition IDs T-n collided with the test-ID scheme; renamed TR-n including in the spec result.
Operability NFR claimed port reporting no acceptance line requires; security NFR cited wrong line for body cap.
Suite live bullet called the class-wide command focused, contradicting the file's own Smoke definition.
Skills bullet repeated focused and full suite runs where smoke and full was meant.
C1 fleet-shape check could not fail: shot sequences do not determine ship lengths when ships touch; also depended on fire after game over.
Check command accepted one merged doc block, though C4 asks for a block per entry point.
TC_BROWSER_WIN stop condition needed a message wording the spec never fixes; now stops on a request-less click.
TC_BROWSER_FIRE required a ready status message the spec does not ask for.
TC_BROWSER_ERROR decided re-enablement from markup rather than behaviour.
RB-6 checked the page.js module instead of the served HTTP body that R-3.1 names.
No check backed the no filesystem or shell use security claim; added static scan to T-8.
AD-4 port parse left under-specified where spec requires Number(PORT) semantics and empty guard order.
Nothing observed that the return actually happened; consumer checks can fall back to the work area.
Target bullet named a worktree tip SHA already invalidated by the pass's own commit.
Deploy step described only the fast-forward, not the working-tree fallback.
Confirm paragraph and table header implied one location for checks that release-check also runs.
Missing blank line glued the cleanup paragraph to the release-verify paragraph.
Check table rows for TC_BROWSER_ERROR, START_FAIL and WIN described behaviour the cases no longer have.
A-R2.3 row pointed at TC_BROWSER_WIN step 4, moved to step 5 by the prior review's rewrite.
W3 status line still said page.js holds seven cases.
environment.md harness description claimed a case-stopped server and a sole reload navigation, untrue of eight cases.
Reserved test-ID list never extended with TC_BROWSER_START_FAIL.
spec A-R2.4 prescribed stopping the server while the case injects failure; open-gap still counted seven browser cases.
T-10 require scan would reject the product's own relative modules that R-1.1 permits.
T-33 scratch test title used a command-level ID, breaking the ID convention and polluting T-31 extraction.
T-32 and T-33 command blocks discarded output, so they could not show their stated expected results.
R-12 and TC-13 did not say shots are sent before reading the first response, so a sequential run passes a racy server.
R-10 mutation check did not name the rule it breaks, so not replayable.
R-18 loopback-only clause had no check; TC-16 covered only port 3000.
TC-5 did not assert 200 and application/json for each valid shot.
TC-6 did not assert application/json for each rejection.
R-9 said server.js handles HTTP only, uncheckable and conflicting with it holding the games.
A-R10.2 named no replayable predicate and the same-coordinates test proves nothing; replaced with a verifiable sequence.
Performance NFR claimed no document reload but no acceptance line backed it; A-R2.2 extended.
lib/game.js header called the logic pure, contradicted by Math.random and record mutation; comment reworded.
R-1 and research decision 10 stated incompatible port rules; spec now records which binds.
withPage ignored Page.navigate errors, so an unreachable origin failed as an uninformative 5 s timeout.
close() after a Chrome crash never settled because no second exit event is emitted.
Launch failure while waiting for DevToolsActivePort leaked the browser-check profile directory.
Failed spawn raised an unhandled error event and fast exits cost the full 20 s deadline.
Removed dead wsPath field.
C-NFR3-1 required exactly one stdout line, stricter than the spec, failing conforming servers.
Rules-module call and fleet shape for deterministic tests were unnamed in plan and architecture.
W1 context did not name the acceptance identifiers its completion covers, only a generic phrase.
TC-3 checked that served HTML has the title, so a longer title would pass; now checks exact title text.
TC-6 did not name the request for each rejection row.
TC-6 repeated-cell row referred to a 409 without sending the second shot.
TC-6 game-over row did not send the shot the 409 applies to.
server.js header lacked the access posture statement (loopback bind, no authentication); added.
Header carried a plan note about later steps that goes stale when S2 lands; removed.
Shell new-game button is unlabelled; left as planned for W3.
Loopback clause omitted ::1, so checkers could disagree.
R-5 said a valid shot returns 200 while R-6 rejects post-game shots with 409; defined valid shot.
R-8 named a game record no check or response carries; words removed.
TC-5 per-cell checks named no fleet or cells, so not replayable; fleet and firing sequence added.
TC-13 second check named no cells for its ten shots; now names (0,0) to (0,9).
Inline code span for workspace return split across a line break; and release-target bullet split.
Closing sentence said non-knowledge paths are kept as if already decided, rather than by the review's --keep.
SYS-TAB expected the tab absent and allowed a name-only PermissionSetTabSetting filter, a false empty.
SYS-UI named no illegal square and no promotion plies.
A4 visibility check (listing CustomTab metadata) does not show who can open the tabs and was a weaker stand-in.
W2 confirm-by omitted the human class command R-9 requires.
Budget-test row said budget item although those methods belong to W1.
R-4 claimed both perft strings omit clocks as published, but position 3 includes 0 1.
Sweep counted only hit and sunk, so a fire body carrying extra properties such as ship cells would pass.
R-6 accepted an import the server never calls.
Restart check assumed port 3000 was free.
Stage result summary held an actual newline flattened by the display; final_result now represents LF literally.
Clarified failure and excluded-behaviour confirmation methods in the spec.
R-5 told HTTP checks to replay a seeded coordinate table the server cannot accept, so the start is unreachable.
R-5 said an unshot cell after gameOver can return sunk; it can only be miss.
R-6 would pass a test that only put R-4 or R-5 in the title.
After New game a click could call applyMove with a move from the stale previous move list.
Square buttons showed only the piece glyph; the coordinate was only in aria-label.
Success body not stated as exactly its keys, so an extra JSON key would pass.
R-6 allowed an R-5 test checking only result and gameOver.
Page could list the same sunk name twice; no rule forbade it.
S3's word every needed explicit limit to successful fires.
TC_8 stopped at the e2e4 FEN, so a bug never clearing en passant on the next move would pass.
TC_4 counted 14 moves without showing omitted clocks default to 0 and 1.
TC_21 named Kiwipete without the FEN string.
TC-2 listener comparison after process exit could pass a server holding an ephemeral port or never exiting.
Promotion results named only the queen, so a wrong suffix still yielding a queen would pass.
En passant capture was specified for white only.
Black promotion case was unstated.
applyMove accepted e2e4q as e2e4 because the promotion character was ignored.
legalMoves accepted side W because Apex == is case-insensitive.
Bad clock threw TypeException instead of IllegalMoveException.
Four public methods had no contract comments.
Three docstring lines exceeded 88 characters; rewrapped.
TC_META treated any SLChess_Board mention as the app tab, and a flexipage with no component would pass.
TC_8 and TC_14 showed ellipsis fragments, so a suffix assertion could stand in for the whole FEN.
R-1 had no check.
TC_5 named castle UCI moves without result FENs.
TC_9 accepted any non-empty list for the check position.
Smoke command had never been run; probe exit recorded.
Consumer check bare node --test exits 0 with zero tests when product absent, so it could not fail.
Invalid-PORT check did not say to stop the unset-PORT server first, so overlap could flake the refused-connection check.
Black rook leaving home lacked a replayable result FEN, so an engine clearing rights only on capture would pass.
Implement result said the status starts as Choose a cell; corrected in the final result for the test stage.
W3 focused command was in environment.md but uncommitted, absent from HEAD.
environment.md misdescribed the request helper signature.
TC_10 said the en passant square is included, which was wrong.
TC_11 named only the first rank of a promotion.
App check allowed a Classic app with Standard navigation.
Rollback used git reset --hard with a placeholder path instead of the documented reset --keep recipe.
Post-release present and absent outputs were claimed but unprobed.
R-4 left the order of validation checks open, so two implementations could differ.
Claim about bare node --test was wrong: it runs helpers.js and loads the opt-in browser file.
TC-13 had no fixed seeds.
TC-16 left TC-15's status open.
Post-release absent signal cannot occur: node --test exits 0 with tests 0, a pass by absence.
AD-3 and AD-4 were filed under Structure rather than Decisions.
No architecture decision carried a status.
R-2 checked only stdout, weaker than R-1's exit code and stderr checks.
R-2 mutation check named no concrete mutation.
cwd check used a <repo> placeholder that cannot be replayed.
spec.md Basis lines carried test ID TC_1, against the rule that test IDs live only in test code.
Examples had no concrete coordinates, so not replayable.
Row/col orientation was unstated.
Server startup method for tests was unspecified.
No 405 behaviour was specified.
Injected layout and rng had no interface.
UI-1 had a garbled sentence and no countable selector.
Test file layout unspecified, so the discovery command was not replayable.
TC_14 exactly-64KiB case named no endpoint or body.
All responses JSON had no assertion.
AD-2 left page location open between inline string and page.html.
ID convention put TC_1 in the method name, which would not count as its own word in -v output.
TC-4 oracle asserted shots count unchanged, a field the contract never defines; replaced with observable state.
